concerns.text: FR-001 says the system MUST 'exclude routine single-command tasks' from the 24-task set, yet US-3 acceptance scenario 2 and SC-002 require distinguishing 'performance gains on complex multi-step tasks versus routine single-step tasks'. If routine tasks are excluded by FR-001, the routine-vs-complex comparison in US-3/SC-002 cannot be performed on the selected task set — a direct contradiction between the task-selection requirement and the analysis requirement.

SC-003 requires measuring a 'false-positive rate of the retrieval mechanism (retrieving irrelevant sequences)' with a <20% threshold, but Constitution Principle VI mandates evaluation rely 'exclusively on the deterministic execution success' and NOT on 'semantic similarity of generated command chains'. Judging whether retrieved sequences are 'irrelevant' requires a semantic-relevance judgment the constitution forbids as an evaluation metric. The spec needs to reconcile SC-003 with Principle VI (e.g., define false-positive retrieval via a deterministic criterion) or drop it.

Terminology drift: US-1 narrative says 'a standard Llama 3 agent' while its acceptance scenario, US-2, FR-002, and the assumptions all say 'Llama 3.1 8B'. Use one consistent model identifier throughout.

SC-005 sweeps top-k over {1,3,5}, implying at least three augmented runs (72 additional task executions), but FR-004 fixes a single 'top-k' retrieval and SC-004 budgets compute for '24 tasks x 2 conditions'. The spec never states whether the k-sweep runs are in scope of the compute budget or additional conditions; clarify to avoid a silent scope shift.
